Conditions that apply: Work to an existing building; Parts with different NCC classes; Building over or next to a water authority asset; Existing on-site detention to keep or modify; Use generates heavy vehicle movements.
Conditions that do not apply: Intersection counts and modelling required.
Conditions not yet known: Works in a public road or intersection; Site fronts or affects a state road; Traffic-generating development referred to TfNSW; Green travel plan required by a condition or the DCP.

Information provided: 12 current documents in the project register, listed in the issue record

### 2. Your role

Traffic engineer for the applicant. You advise the design team on access, parking and circulation while the design develops, and prepare the traffic report the consent authority needs. Plans come from the architect in DWG and PDF.
Design vehicle: B-double
Controls: Strathfield DCP parking rates · Development application (DA)

### 3. Scope by stage

Price each stage that applies as a lump sum; surveys are priced per location. Options are priced on their own and are not in the base fee.

| Stage | Deliverable at sign-off |
|---|---|
| Parking and access advice | Site inspection; review of plans and controls; advice on access, heavy vehicle circulation, loading and parking layout |
| Traffic and parking report | Traffic generation and distribution; network impact (using the modelling stage where it applies); parking provision against the DCP and demand; access and AS 2890 compliance; swept paths for the design vehicle; pedestrian, cyclist and end-of-trip review; safety. 1 draft, 1 final |
| Assessment response | Up to 1 response(s) to council or TfNSW requests; 1 meeting(s) |
| Conditions review | Review of the traffic conditions in the consent; reply letter if needed |
| Construction traffic management plan | Construction traffic management plan for council approval, or review of the contractor's plan (say which in R2); traffic control plans |
| Review of the developed design (option) | Ramps, parking and loading checked against the consent conditions as the design develops or the contractor changes it; signage and line-marking submissions to the local traffic committee. The client opts in. |
| Car park certification (option) | Design certification of the car park, access and loading against AS 2890 for the construction certificate; completed car park certification after construction. The client opts in. |
| Green travel plan (option) | Travel plan meeting the condition or DCP requirement. Price as an option: needed only if a consent condition or the DCP requires a travel plan. |

### 4. Allowances

Price exactly these. Work beyond an allowance needs a written instruction (section 6) and is then charged at your R3 rates.

| Item | Allowance | Item | Allowance |

| Plan revisions assessed | 1 | Report drafts | 1 draft, 1 final |

| Authority responses | 1 | Authority meetings | 1 |

### 5. Scope position

Service levels are set for a complex project (Use generates heavy vehicle movements); technical items follow the project's own facts.
Included in the fee: Vehicle schedule (waste, emergency, service and operator vehicles); ramps, gradients, headroom, sight lines and pedestrian conflicts checked against the current architect and civil layouts; Consultation with council traffic engineers and TfNSW while preparing the report; Bicycle parking and end-of-trip assessment; Parking demand reduction measures; Swept paths for every loading dock and design vehicle.
Optional: price each on its own line in R1: Alternative schemes tested; Road safety audit by an auditor independent of the design team; state its stage and scope in R2 (an audit is needed only for works in a public road).
Excluded: the party named does it: Microsimulation beyond SIDRA (not required); Design of works in the public road (signals, intersections) (civil engineer (separate engagement), to be appointed); Expert witness, Land and Environment Court (client (separate engagement)).
Tell us in R6 if you disagree with any line. Do not add your own general exclusions; any you add are treated as non-compliant.

### 6. Terms

- Engagement is under AS 4122-2010 as amended by the client's special conditions (attached); your own terms do not apply. List any change you propose to the agreement in R6.
- Only a written instruction from the client's representative authorises extra scope, work beyond an allowance or a fee change; work without one is not paid.
- Each stage ends at client sign-off, which sets the baseline for later stages. Design development within the brief is not a variation; a client change after sign-off is assessed under the agreement.
- Correcting your own errors, or coordinating with information you were given, is not a variation.
- Invoice monthly against stage progress; payment within 30 days, not dependent on any authority approval.
- Your proposal stays valid for 90 days.
- Questions in writing to Project manager, pm@example.com by 2026-10-23; answers go to every tenderer as numbered addenda.
- No commencement payment; the final report is not held back pending payment.

### 7. Evaluation

Price 40% · Relevant experience 20% · Team 20% · Methodology and program 10% · Compliance with the returnable schedules 10%. Lowest price does not automatically win.

### Before issue — resolve or accept

**Rules await owner review**: The traffic and parking services rules are a draft. Drafting and editing work; issue stays blocked until the owner marks them reviewed.

**Blocks issue — Gross floor area: sources disagree (2135 vs 2895)**: Set the one figure every firm prices from.

**Green travel plan required by a condition or the DCP: not established**: Priced on a printed assumption until confirmed: Green travel plan.

**Works in a public road or intersection: not established**: Priced on a printed assumption until confirmed: Road safety audit by an auditor independent of the design team; state its stage and scope in R2.
